title: What Loving Me Actually Looks Like
hook: Two lists of acts someone could see or hear. Words, gestures, and behaviors. No type, and no score.
steps: About ten minutes apart. Two items in each row, from life with this person: a visible or audible act, not a bin such as quality time.
Mark every line: already happens, I did not know, or hard for me. Hard is a limit, not a verdict on the wish.
Circle a shape that shows up on both lists. A circle is a poor compatibility score. Difference is a map of you two.
Rewrite a request for a new personality as a behavior, or cross it out. Each of you names one surprise, then stops.
ending: One surprise is a full result. Every line may be declined.
pass: Pass a row, or pause. One item per row is a finished session.
safety: No touch is demonstrated here. If a harm needs to stop, say that plainly, in another conversation.

title: The Appreciation Avalanche
hook: Three rounds of thanks, each harder to aim at a stranger. After every line: I heard that.
steps: Round one is one obvious true sentence. No joke, no compliment returned at once, and no debate about deserving it.
Round two uses a real scene from the last month. If you have no scene, say so. Do not invent a memory.
Round three names one small behavior a hurried person would miss. If you would have to invent it, stop.
Keep the counts equal. A fourth line only if it arrives unhunted. You may repeat one true line, slowly.
ending: Ask if that small behavior should continue. I heard that was not a promise. Yes, no, or sometimes.
pass: No true line means you say so and stop. Two honest rounds are a whole session.
safety: Skip the backhand, the stereotype, and any score for specificity. Thanks do not cover a live harm. A body comment only if that attention was already welcomed.

title: The Moment I Knew
hook: Tell when the other person started to matter more, from your side. A thunderbolt is optional. Accumulation counts.
steps: Give it a place, a shift, and the sentence you did not say then. If it accumulated, name a few ordinary repeats and when you noticed.
The listener asks one question about the teller's experience, and saves their own version for their turn.
One story each. A second story is shorter, and it deepens. It does not replace a first story that felt small.
Say where the memories differ, and leave both standing. Title each scene in six words or fewer.
ending: It accumulated is a complete story. You do not owe a cinematic origin.
pass: You may pass. I do not have a distinct moment is a full opening. Pain may stay one narrow slice.
safety: Skip a story that reviews the other person's improvement. Do not humiliate someone who is absent. A sentence tonight is information, not a bill.

title: Instructions for Loving Me
hook: Each of you writes how you run: operating notes, warning signs, and maintenance. Specific, and due to expire.
steps: Two needs, as situations with a time and a texture. Two tells a person could see, and no diagnosis. Two maintenance items. At least one is yours alone.
Read one manual at a time. One curious question. Say which maintenance you can support. Nobody edits the other page.
Time, money, or a body makes the need a request, and it may be declined. Your signs are not a license to monitor.
Date the page. Pick the maintenance to recheck in six months, and name the day.
ending: A portrait, not a vow and not a grade. One item under each heading is enough.
pass: A line may stay on your page, unread. On a crowded day, the thin manual finishes the session.
safety: Write signs about yourself. A page for managing your partner is out. If the sign is harm, name it in plain language, apart from this manual.

title: The Compliment You Can't Dodge
hook: One concrete compliment, about ten quiet seconds, and a thank-you that stays. This is practice, not a new personality.
steps: The giver says one true, specific line, then stops. Something they did, or a quality already welcomed. You are perfect is a cloud.
Ten seconds. Notice the joke, the argument, the shrug, or the instant return. Then one sentence: Thank you. I am letting that in.
Correct a wrong fact only after that sentence. A compliment handed back in the same breath is a dodge. Swap.
The full sitting is two each. The second line is its own scene, not a receipt. Name the dodge you postponed, with no apology.
ending: After that, ordinary manners may return, joke included, if you label the return.
pass: Pass when a line feels unsafe or simply wrong. Another line, or the turn ends. Do not grade the thank-you.
safety: Appearance, weight, disability, race, gender, and anything sexual stay out unless that kind was already welcomed. Pressure fakes a landing.
